Cheng: quick sync — ran an apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic for kernel-selector branch (kernel-opt-v4). seeing a KV warmup regression on dedicated pools after ~60-90s. short thread with logs and questions.
Maya: can you paste the exact bench command + the minimal numbers?
Cheng: sure — ran replay harness w/ same client traffic profile as prod. command: ```./tools/run_replay --profile=prod.traffic --model=gptx-16k --kernel-profile=kernel-opt-v4 --pool=dedicated-4g``` Results snapshot (baseline -> opt-v4): P50 22ms -> 24ms, P95 310ms -> 348ms, q99 420ms -> 520ms.
Sasha: interesting. did you force batching heuristics to match? small batch shapes can kill KV reuse. how did you set max_batch_size / max_latency?
Cheng: I used bench defaults to mirror prod: max_batch_size=64, max_latency_ms=8. Also ran a variant with max_latency_ms=20 and saw P95 drop back ~6% but still worse than baseline.
Brian: any difference across pool sizing? dedicated-4g vs dedicated-8g? burst credits behavior could mask scale-up differences.
Cheng: good call — on 8g pool the cold-start tail is less bad but warmup still sits ~8% higher. Logs show KV hit-rate climbs slower under opt-v4. snippet: ```KVCache: hit_rate=0.12 @t=30s -> 0.48 @t=120s (baseline) vs 0.06 -> 0.35 (opt-v4)```
Maya: that hit_rate delta would explain extra token work. could kernel change be changing key layout or implicit padding so cache keys don't match? any model sharding changes?
Sasha: I saw a small packing change in the selector where sequence-grouping was tightened (to reduce useless padding), which can change prefix alignment across requests and reduce contiguous KV reuse.
Cheng: confirmed — kernel-opt-v4 introduced grouping heuristic that packs smaller sequences together. it reduced avg tokens/completion by 3% but seems to fragment KV cache.
Brian: two routes: revert grouping or add a KV-friendly grouping mode behind a flag. also run an apples-to-apples where only kernel selector differs (no batching heuristics) so we isolate impact.
Cheng: on it. I'll run a targeted replay where we force the old grouping + new kernels. planning tests: (1) replay w/ old grouping + opt-v4 kernels, (2) replay w/ new grouping + baseline kernels, (3) synthetic mix to validate.
InfraBot: Created internal perf issue PERF-1429 and attached current logs.
Maya: please include: scale-up timeline (time-to-ready instance), burst-credit usage during spikes, KV miss distribution by sequence length bucket. that will help understand autoscale interplay.
Cheng: will post results ASAP. initial hypothesis: grouping reduced wasted tokens but harmed cross-request KV coalescing; that lowers hit rate and increases backend kernel time which surfaces as higher P95.
Sasha: also watch batch shape heatmap — if batch shapes became wider but shorter (more diverse lengths), batching efficiency drops. quick command: ```./tools/shape_heatmap --trace=lastrun```
Brian: thanks — if we confirm, let's gate grouping behind an autoscale-aware heuristic so dedicated pools keep predictable tail.
Maya: 👍 and ping me when you have the targeted replay numbers, we should triage before the next rollout window.
Cheng: will update with the three runs (timestamps + logs) in this thread. thanks all.
